pr_title: Fix Culture creation regression when using invalid names on Windows
pr_body:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/57310

This change is fixing a regression from .NET 5.0. The problem happens when trying to create a CultureInfo object using culture names that Windows don't allow. 
This regression occurred during the code refactoring work done to optimize the globalization data size and WASM support.
Although this fix is addressing the regression, it fixes another issue I have discovered during the investigation. Here is what the change is doing:
- In the file `CultureData.Windows.cs`, the condition `ShouldUseUserOverrideNlsData` is wrong to use. The reason is this part of the code is not concerned about the user overrides. Even the user overrides flag is not initialized yet at this stage.
- In the same file, I added the call to Windows API `GetLocaleInfoEx` that help validate the culture name. That is what we have done in .NET 5.0 too.
- In the file `IcuLocaleData.cs`, there was a bug that caused not finding the proper culture name mapping to our data because the culture name containing characters like underscore character `_`.
- Fixing and adding tests.

issue_context.title: [.NET 6] CultureInfo constructor does not throw CultureNotFoundException for unknown culture name
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

In .NET 5 and older versions of .NET Core and Framework this code throws `CultureNotFoundException` ("Culture is not supported" message).

`CultureInfo culture = new CultureInfo("broken");`

In .NET 6 it does not throw and creates a `CultureInfo` instance with "broken" name.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3258785/129255853-57b8a248-71bf-4b0d-8a94-bc02832dfeb0.png)

When adding an unknown region component, the constructor still succeeds, but `CompareInfo` property starts throwing `CultureNotFoundException`.

`CultureInfo culture = new CultureInfo("broken-CULTURE");`

The resulting culture's name is "broken--CULTURE".

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3258785/129256804-48f97b30-2e5d-48af-be10-e171e48a7ad2.png)

### Configuration
.NET versions: .NET 6 preview 6 and 7. Did not test earlier previews.
OS: latest versions of Windows 10 and 11 with OS language set to English (United States).
Architecture: x64.
All other parameters are set to default, this reproes on a new console app on a fresh Windows installation.

### Regression?

I did not find any breaking change notifications in public documentation for `CultureInfo` in .NET 6.
